title: The runtime tree accounts for all wall time
body:
The `-s` runtime tree had two branches, seeding and alignment. Neither the top level nor the seeding branch summed to its wall. Query indexing, target indexing and `build_pipeline` were untimed, or timed with the duration thrown away. The mmseqs db writes and the bookkeeping of progressive seeding fell into seeding's `[misc.]`. The alignment leaves printed sums of thread time, which read as a bug beside the branch wall.

The milestone is done when the leaves of every branch plus its `[misc.]` sum to the branch wall, runtime equals the sum of the branches, and the alignment leaves show derived wall time.

## Proposal

The format was settled on 2026-09-28. The tree stays, and extra data points go in square brackets. Only the alignment branch gets a column header, with a dashed rule on the tree rail. There is no new output file, no event log and no timestamps. The target tree is in the notes.

Behavior does not change, except that `build_pipeline` moves ahead of `seed()`. The progress `println!`s in `search.rs` stay as feedback for the user.

## Out of scope

- `--stats-results-path` was validated and never written. Commit `432ff65` removed it.
close_reason: A full run in progressive seeding mode at `41781f9` checks all four conditions: 20,795 Pfam profiles against 2,455,940 targets at `-t 8`, 707.51 s. Seeding misc is 0.74 s of 250.51 s. Setup 0.86 s, seeding 250.51 s, alignment 456.05 s and root misc 0.09 s sum to the runtime. The align leaf prints 11 readable iteration rows. The derived alignment walls sum to 456.04 s against the branch wall of 456.05 s, at 98.4% busy. The full tree is note a90458b8 on nail-1964b2.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/415c993d
notes.text:
Target tree, with illustrative numbers. The serial branches keep their shape, and only alignment gets the header and rule.

```text
runtime: 557.31s
 └─ setup:       9.20s ( 1.65%)
     ├─ query index          1.02s
     ├─ target index         2.10s
     ├─ pipeline build       5.93s
     └─ [misc.]              0.15s
 └─ seeding:   347.02s (62.27%)
     ├─ db write             4.11s
     ├─ prefilter          289.40s
     ├─ align               36.04s   [4 iterations]
     │   ├─ 1                3.10s
     │   ├─ 2                6.22s
     │   ├─ 3               12.40s
     │   └─ 4               14.32s
     ├─ convertalis          2.80s
     ├─ seed index           1.20s
     └─ [misc.]              1.47s
 └─ alignment: 201.34s (36.13%)   [48 threads, cpu 9,610s, 99.4% busy]
     │                        wall        %      cpu
     │                     -------   ------   ------
     ├─ cloud search       113.02s   56.13%   5,425s
     ├─ backward            34.20s   16.99%   1,642s
     ├─ forward             29.10s   14.45%   1,397s
     ├─ posterior            9.31s    4.62%     447s
     ├─ optimal accuracy     8.02s    3.98%     385s
     └─ [misc.]              7.69s    3.82%     369s
 └─ [misc.]      0.75s ( 0.13%)
```

The alignment leaves show share × wall, with no idle row. A parallel run has no measurable wall per stage, so a leaf's wall is a definition. Share × wall spreads any idle time over the leaves in proportion, where cpu ÷ threads would show idle as its own row. At full use the two agree, and the busy figure on the branch line already says how much idle there is. Decided 2026-09-28.

This milestone started from a handoff written in `nail-benchmarks` under `benchmarks/stage-times` on 2026-09-28, against `837ba60`. The handoff proposed a phase event log with timestamps, written through `--stats-results-path`, and that mechanism was rejected. The gaps it found are what this milestone closes.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/415c993d
notes.text:
All four children are on `dev`, fast-forwarded to `8d8153e`, and `432ff65` removed `--stats-results-path`. The milestone stays open until a real run in progressive seeding mode with mmseqs checks four things:

- seeding's `[misc.]` is small
- the branches sum to runtime
- the iteration rows are readable
- the derived alignment walls sum to the branch wall, with busy near 100%
